HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• Presenting complaint: Dry cough, runny nose, myalgias, intermittent headache and chills for ~5 days (since start of weekend).  
• Character: Dry, “hacking” cough; no sputum or hemoptysis.  
• Associated symptoms: Nasal congestion, mild sore throat (pharyngeal redness noted), muscle aches, chills.  
• Negative symptoms: No shortness of breath, no wheeze, no chest pain, no neck gland swelling noted by patient.  
• Self-care to date: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented). No ibuprofen.  
• Triggers/relievers: None reported. First similar episode this season.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus × 5–6 years.  
• Hypertension (mild).  
• Medications:  
  – Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  – Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  – Paracetamol PRN for current symptoms – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• Monitoring: Home blood glucose “within normal,” BP checked this morning “normal” (values not provided).  
• Surgical/Hospital history: Not discussed.

Physical Examination:  (video-consult findings)
• General: Appears well; breathing comfortably.  
• HEENT: Mild erythema of posterior pharynx; tonsils not enlarged. No visible cervical lymphadenopathy.  
• Respiratory: No wheeze or audible rattles; patient denies dyspnea.  
• Cardiovascular, Abdomen, Neuro, Skin: Not examined/reported.

Impression:
Uncomplicated viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold).

Management Plan:
• Supportive care: Advise OTC combination cold remedies (Day Nurse/Night Nurse) deemed safe with current medications; continue paracetamol as needed.  
• Red-flag advice: Seek medical review if shortness of breath, wheeze, chest tightness, persistent fever, or if symptoms last > 3 weeks or significantly worsen.  
• Medications: No prescription required today; continue metformin and lisinopril as usual.  
• Follow-up: PRN via GP or urgent care if red-flag symptoms occur. Routine review not necessary if symptoms resolve.

Patient Summary:
Mr. John Jones, 43-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and mild hypertension, presents with a 5-day history of dry cough and cold symptoms without respiratory compromise. Examination is reassuring for a viral URTI; no treatment beyond symptomatic relief is indicated. He was counselled on OTC options and warning signs.

Key Takeaways:
1. Use Day Nurse/Night Nurse or paracetamol for symptom relief as needed.  
2. Return if breathless, wheezy, or if symptoms persist beyond three weeks or worsen.  
3. Continue regular diabetes and blood-pressure medications.

Next Steps:
• Self-monitor symptoms; maintain hydration and rest.  
• Contact GP/urgent care if red-flag symptoms develop.  
• Routine diabetes/BP follow-up through usual care pathways.
